sec: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rule · p831

items.q: The most abundant source of serotonin is:
items.exp: Serotonin's most abundant source is the enterochromaffin cells of the GIT; melatonin's is the pineal gland. (Book p831)

items.q: The most abundant source of melatonin is:
items.exp: Melatonin's most abundant source is the pineal gland. (Book p831)

items.q: ‘Serotonin and melatonin act as centrally-acting neurotransmitters and peripherally-acting hormones.’
items.exp: Both are centrally acting neurotransmitters and peripherally acting hormones. (Book p831)

items.q: In the sleep–wake cycle, the transmitter that keeps us alert and active is:
items.exp: Serotonin keeps us alert and active; melatonin helps in sleep. (Book p831)

items.q: At night (9:30–10 pm) light signals fall. What happens to serotonin and melatonin respectively?
items.exp: At night, reduced light signals lower serotonin, allowing melatonin to rise (gradual, maximum at 2–2:30 am). (Book p831)

items.q: Melatonin levels reach their maximum at about:
items.exp: Melatonin rises gradually at night with maximum levels at 2–2:30 am. (Book p831)

items.q: A teenager overuses gadgets at night. The downstream consequence that can ultimately result is:
opts: Depression, via disrupted serotonin and a sleep–wake cycle that cannot raise melatonin
items.exp: Gadget overuse at night keeps serotonin up so melatonin cannot rise, disrupting the sleep–wake cycle and serotonin levels, which can lead to depression. (Book p831)

items.q: Match the ‘hormones of happiness’ (DOSE) — D  O  S  E … A) Oxytocin  B) Endorphins  C) Dopamine  D) Serotonin
items.exp: DOSE = Dopamine, Oxytocin, Serotonin, Endorphins. (Book p831)

items.q: By the 80/20 rule, the adrenal gland is composed of cortex and medulla in the ratio:
items.exp: The adrenal gland is 80% cortex and 20% medulla. (Book p831)

items.q: Within the adrenal medulla, adrenaline and noradrenaline are secreted in the ratio:
items.exp: The medulla secretes 80% adrenaline and 20% noradrenaline. (Book p831)
